editorial:
Imagine being pushed to your absolute limit by a classmate who makes your life a living nightmare. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow a small group of high school kids in Florida who are tired of being pushed around by Bobby, a mean bully who treats them like garbage. Instead of going to a teacher or their parents, they decide to take matters into their own hands. The vibe is raw and uncomfortable because it feels like you are spying on real teenagers rather than watching actors in a movie. It captures that scary feeling of being young and making a huge mistake because you feel trapped.

What really hits hard is the acting; the kids feel totally authentic and not like they are reading from a script. The pacing is slow at first, building up a lot of tension before everything goes wrong. If you like dark stories that show the ugly side of growing up, you will find this gripping. It is not a happy movie, but it stays with you. You can rent it on Apple TV if you want a quick watch, or you might want to add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The plot to kill Bobby goes horribly wrong and becomes a messy, violent disaster. After the murder, the group tries to cover their tracks and act like nothing happened. However, the guilt and the police investigation quickly catch up to them. You see the group fall apart as they turn on each other. In the end, they are all arrested, showing that their attempt to escape the bullying only led to a much worse fate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty dramas about the dark side of youth.
